I could find nothing to say.

What had happened between Ayane and her father?
I could imagine some of it—or thought I could. Yet it still seemed impossibly far away.

en.html:
She did not sound as if she were evading me.
Ichijou truly had no answer. And, judging by her expression, she was not seeking one.

Perhaps she could not yet look directly at that past.
If she looked back, the answer would be there. She knew that.
That was why she could not look back.

It would be like digging a nail into a wound that had never healed.

Was her letting me glimpse part of that wound a sign that our conversation had somehow had a positive effect?

I could only wonder.
Pursuing the matter out of curiosity would achieve nothing.
Besides, even what she had said was enough to tell me something.

　それはきっと、癒えぬ傷跡へ爪を立てることなのだ。

がしかの<ruby>正<rt>プラス</rt></ruby>作用を一条に及ぼしたから、で、あろうか。

　興味本位の追及は無益だ。
　それに、今の話だけでもわかる事がある。

en.html:
Yes.

This girl was the same as me.

She had killed the parent she loved above all others, and after that there was no turning back.

Parricide had cursed her life.

...Now I could see it. The twist in this girl's mind. Where her clinging to "justice" came from.

If that road had been opened with her father's blood, she could neither deny it nor retreat from it. To do so would make worthless a sacrifice too heavy and too precious.

The same as me.

I do not like the word fate; it smells of running away. But the meeting of Ichijou and me may deserve exactly that name.

A father-killer and a mother-killer, meeting.

...If this is truly what they call fate, then where does it finally carry us?

en.html:
Her voice grew smaller and smaller, then hoarse, and at the end it melted into the sound of her sleeping breath.

—Was that right?

I turned the melted question over. I chewed it inside my skull and weighed it carefully.

Was that right?

...Was it?

To hate evil, raise the banner of justice, and punish it.

That should not be wrong. It ought to be right.

Justice. Spoken by this girl of all people, I can believe it.

In judging good and evil she is entirely selfless. Her verdicts are strict, frighteningly so.

Even the killing of Doushin Yusa. If it caused any trouble, the trouble was political only. As for right and wrong, Ichijou's justice was clear.

That is what I think.

And yet.

Truly, though. Was that right?

...No answer came. However long I thought, I could not produce one.

ja.html:
一条の声は次第に小さく、やがてかすれて。
　最後は寝息の中に溶けて消えた。

　――<ruby>それ<rt>・・</rt></ruby>でいいのか。

　溶けた問いかけを反芻する。
　脳漿の中で噛み砕き、慎重に吟味する。

　それでいいのか。
　
　……いいのか？

　悪を憎み。
　正義を掲げてそれを罰する。

　それは――間違ってはいない筈だ。
　正しい――筈だ。

　正義。
　他ならぬこの少女が語るなら信じられる。

　彼女は善悪の判断において全く無私だ。
　厳正極まる裁きを下す。空恐ろしい程に。

　遊佐童心の殺害とて。
　不都合があるとすればそれはただ政略的にであって、
理非を問うなら一条の正しさは明らかだ。

　そう思う。
　
　だが。

　本当に。
　<ruby>それでいいのか<rt>・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>？

　……答えは出ない。
　いくら考えても、俺はその答えを出せなかった。
